correctness.rationale: Using the exact cycle Lie brackets, the Kirillov form has a 2n-dimensional alternating block with off-diagonal n-by-n mixed matrix D. It is invertible exactly if D is invertible; if D is singular the alternating rank is at most 2n-2. Its support graph splits into gcd(n,3) bipartite cycles, giving determinant zero when 3 does not divide n and a product of three residue-class product differences when 3 divides n; C3 is proved separately. Explicit t choices realize full D rank over fields with more than two elements at divisible lengths, and corank one in all remaining cases including F2. Counting triples of pairwise distinct block products proves the exact finite-field count. The checker verifies 64 witnesses, 6419 exhaustive central assignments and 12730 full noncentral cases; finite checks are not treated as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 construction contains cyclic graph brackets and center dimensions but not a Kirillov index or central-radical enumerator. The closest 2025 graph index theorem applies to the distinct Dani--Mainkar two-step algebra. Existing complete-bipartite work covers the special case C4=K2,2, not the infinitely many other cycle lengths or the finite-field functional enumeration. Searches for aliases, coadjoint rank, and cyclic three-step constructions did not reveal a dominating theorem. This is a best-knowledge assessment, not uniqueness certification.

value.rationale: Kirillov index is a standard nontrivial coadjoint invariant, not fixed by the center dimension. The complete infinite-cycle classification exhibits a mod-three obstruction and an exceptional field-size jump between F2 and F4 that cannot be inferred from characteristic alone. The exact finite-field count quantifies the space of center-minimal stabilizers, with potential relevance to orbit distributions; it is not merely a numerical small-case test.
